name: Can open-floor-plan conversions work in small homes?

mainEntity.name: Are open-floor-plan conversions worth it in smaller Los Angeles homes or condos?
mainEntity.text: Are open-floor-plan conversions worth it in smaller Los Angeles homes or condos?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open plans can work very well in smaller homes because they improve light, circulation, and the sense of space. However, they can also backfire if the remodel removes the only place for storage, TV placement, or quiet separation. In compact Los Angeles homes, the best designs usually use selective openings, built-ins, islands, or defined zones instead of removing every barrier. For condos or attached housing, structure, HOA rules, and utility access may also shape what is possible. A smart small-home conversion should be measured against how the space will be used every day, not just how it looks in photos. The goal is to gain openness without losing livability.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but only if the opening improves function instead of creating a single oversized room. In small homes, the design must protect storage, privacy, and furniture placement while making the space feel brighter and larger.
